title: Area and volume for jobs
log: 2026-11-01T14:46:39Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new

match.reason: No bank point covers estimating paint, tiles or concrete for a job with waste allowance, and none covers compound solids, so the bank's basic area and volume cards don't teach this idea.

draft.title: Area and volume for jobs
card: Split a compound shape into simple shapes such as rectangles and triangles. Find each area, then add them. Perimeter is the total length around the outside.
Volume of a rectangular prism = length × width × height. Concrete for a slab is its volume, so all three lengths must be in the same unit, such as metres.
1 m³ = 1000 litres, and 1 m² = 10 000 cm². Convert before you multiply.
Allow for waste by adding a percentage. Example: 40 m² of tiles plus 10% waste is 40 × 1.1 = 44 m².
draft.remember: Split into simple shapes, keep units the same, then add the waste allowance last.

a.q: An L-shaped floor is made from a 6 m by 4 m rectangle and a 2 m by 3 m rectangle. What is its area?
a.why: Area = 6 × 4 + 2 × 3 = 24 + 6 = 30 m². The option 24 m² leaves out the second rectangle.
a.clue: Find each rectangle's area, then add.

b.q: Sam pours a concrete slab 5 m long, 4 m wide and 0.1 m thick in Bendigo. He orders 10% extra. How much concrete does he order?
b.why: Volume = 5 × 4 × 0.1 = 2 m³. Adding 10% gives 2 × 1.1 = 2.2 m³. The option 2.1 m³ adds 0.1 instead of 10% of the volume.
b.clue: Find the volume first, then add 10% of it.
